findings.body: The route guard runs only through resolvePermissionIpcDecision. In ipc-interaction-processing.ts:228–237, a persisted approval short-circuits that function, so an active run can receive an approved response after its conversation route or binding is removed. New evidence beyond the earlier route ruling is the changed restart fixture in ipc-interaction-handler.test.ts:2708 and 2807–2863: it supplies a live run binding but no conversationRoutes, then expects a transient grant and signed allow. Check the route before replaying either persisted approval mode, while preserving the recorded human answer, and cover route removal on this replay path.
findings.title: Not done: route checks precede persisted approvals

findings.body: The T2-owned gaps remain: runner/permission-ipc-client.ts:179 transports toolUseID, and ipc-parsing.ts:483 does not populate invocationId. The Claude duplicate client remains, with runner/job-heartbeat.ts:6 reading its pending requests. Protected-path and YOLO checks also remain in the Claude tool-permission-gate.ts:324 and 380. T2 must transport engine ids, consolidate the client and runner checks, and prove that the shared client's pending requests appear in job heartbeats. This remains nonblocking for T1 under the task ownership and transport ruling.
findings.title: Later: finish invocation transport and runner consolidation in T2

findings.body: The T3-owned coverage remains incomplete: registry.ts:575–580 gates only delegation tools; DeepAgents runner/mcp-tools.ts:158–164 returns selected Gantry tools without the common permission wrapper; and the Claude inline lane still allows core tools at inline-lane/index.ts:178–192. Dispatcher consultation still passes the dispatcher name unchanged at ipc-permission-classifier-decision.ts:276. T3 must complete these entries and resolved-target decisions, the four-engine chat/job/mode table, actual one-ask alias versus two-call proof, and deepagents-gantry-tool-gate, which is absent from test/e2e. The host pinning and three-caller tests do not replace that assigned engine proof. This is nonblocking for T1.
findings.title: Later: complete engine gate coverage and its proof in T3

findings.body: The T4-owned gaps remain: unsupported shapes ask before the judge under the temporary rail ruling; permission-classifier.ts:360 skips consultation when auto_strict lacks read-only proof; ipc-parsing.ts:447–454 sanitizes before rail evaluation without a complete program/path summary; gantry-tool-risk.ts:70–71 fixes capability_run as high risk; and structured-local-cli-invocation.ts:170–173 still refuses template mismatches. T4 must supply the shape/danger table, beyond-cut danger/path and malformed-input cases, repeated/restarted template-mismatch allow/deny cases, piped/chained Postgres proof, and piped-command-judge-allow, which is absent from test/e2e. This remains nonblocking for T1 and does not challenge its approved temporary rail policy.
findings.title: Later: finish command policy and its proof in T4
